To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
the DNA-binding domain of transcription factor Stat 3 is located within amino acids 406–432, and that the 32-kDA tryptic fragment is capable of sequence-specific DNA-binding.

the transcription factor Stat3 is a dimeric protein, the two monomers of which are connected by disulfide bridges and that each monomer contains a DNA-binding domain of 100–110 amino acids that can be proteolytically released from the intact factor.

a 32-kDa fragment of Stat3, generated by partial proteolytic digestion with trypsin and containing a major portion of the sequence-specific DNA-binding domain (amino acids, 406–514) and the SH2 and SH3 domains, retains sequence-specific DNA-binding ability.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the identification of minimal DNA-binding domains of transcription factor Stat 3 by partial proteolyses.
the elucidation of the structure of the transcription factor Stat3 and its complexes with DNA.
the elucidation of the DNA-binding domain of transcription factor Stat-3.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
a 32-kDa fragment of Stat3 containing the DNA-binding domain and the tyrosine phosphorylation site is sufficient for DNA binding.
the DNA-binding domain of the 94-kDa Stat3 is located between amino acids 406 and 514.
the DNA-binding domain of transcription factor Stat 3 is a fragment of 32 kDa.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that

the DNA-binding domain of the transcription factor Stat3 is a 75-kDa protein containing the N-terminal part of the DNA-binding domain (amino acids (aa) 406–514) and the SH2 and SH3 domains, but not the last 20 amino acids (aa 515–534).
the DNA-binding domain of transcription factor Stat 3 is a 100 amino acid stretch containing the SH2 and the phosphorylated Tyr 705.

the DNA-binding domain of transcription factor Stat 3 consists of the sequence 406–514, that the SH2 domain is not essential for sequence-specific DNA binding but may stabilize the complex, and that the SH3 domain may be required for the interaction with DNA.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the minimal DNA-binding fragment of Stat3 is only 32 kDa.

the DNA-binding domain of a transcription factor can be defined by partial proteolys is of the intact protein and that the DNA-binding fragments generated in this way may be suitable for crystallization.
the DNA-binding domain of the transcription factor Stat3 is capable of specific DNA binding as a 32-kDa proteolytic fragment.
